software-feature-contracts.name: Three model features arrive out of order
software-feature-contracts.prompt: Botie now receives c, a and b, while the model expects a, b and c. Predict the weighted sum before connecting the new record.
software-feature-contracts.why: The adapter must use the supplied schema rather than a hard-coded reversal of two fields.

software-fitted-state.name: Negative readings on a new device
software-fitted-state.prompt: The fitted device saw negative readings. Predict the transformed request without centring it on its own mean.
software-fitted-state.why: The reference may be negative. Its ownership matters more than the sign of the measurements.

software-retrieval-shortlists.name: The best scores are both negative
software-retrieval-shortlists.prompt: All three similarities are below zero, and two passages tie. Predict the shortlist using relative order rather than a positive-score assumption.
software-retrieval-shortlists.why: Negative scores still have an ordering; equal scores must preserve the incoming positions.

software-workflow-dependencies.name: A job has no prerequisites
software-workflow-dependencies.prompt: One waiting job needs no prior result, another needs the second prerequisite, and the last needs both. Predict readiness after only the first completes.
software-workflow-dependencies.why: A zero-dependency row is ready immediately, while unrelated completion still cannot satisfy another row.

software-named-request-contracts.name: A Boolean reaches the vibration field
software-named-request-contracts.prompt: Botie receives a flag, a negative reading and an omitted vibration. Predict both aligned lists before testing.
software-named-request-contracts.why: The rule must inspect types and key presence, not memorise a temperature fixture.

software-schema-evolution.name: A future version has familiar-looking fields
software-schema-evolution.prompt: The new fixture declares version 3 but uses query/count. Predict whether familiar keys are enough to make it supported.
software-schema-evolution.why: A contract version is an explicit promise, not a guess from a similar object shape.

software-semantic-contracts.name: A different Fahrenheit batch and fitted coefficient
software-semantic-contracts.prompt: The incoming readings are 32 F and 77 F. The model has a 10 C centre and coefficient 0.5. Predict the two scores before testing.
software-semantic-contracts.why: A complete conversion must handle the offset and changed model state, rather than hard-code the earlier scores.

software-tool-errors.name: A new code arrives beside an uncertain outcome
software-tool-errors.prompt: The service adds an unrecognised code. Predict both actions with no remaining retry budget.
software-tool-errors.why: Unknown failure types must not become a newly invented automatic recovery protocol.

software-contract-tests.name: A different first reading shares the busy batch
software-contract-tests.prompt: The new first reading is 6, followed by 100 and 2. The stored centre remains 4, and the independent first-result expectation is 2. Predict both outputs.
software-contract-tests.why: The construction must preserve fitted state and follow the current first example rather than remember a previous position’s value.

data-partition-statistics.name: Three workers, including an empty one
data-partition-statistics.prompt: Botie receives three partition reports. Keep the empty worker from changing either the denominator or the weighting of the other records.
data-partition-statistics.why: The summary must retain counts across additional partitions, empty inputs and negative readings.

data-asof-features.name: A feature arrives exactly at the cutoff
data-asof-features.prompt: The inclusive policy permits equality. Predict the surviving values when one record arrives at the decision and another arrives a moment later.
data-asof-features.why: Boundary equality must be deliberate, while an earlier event still cannot excuse a late arrival.

data-contract-quarantine.name: Valid boundary readings surround one failure
data-contract-quarantine.prompt: Both interval endpoints are valid. Predict the accepted sequence and rejected count without sorting or changing the original readings.
data-contract-quarantine.why: The mask must preserve record order and accept both boundaries while reporting the excluded row.

data-stream-windows.name: Out-of-order events meet two boundaries
data-stream-windows.prompt: The input is not sorted. Predict which readings belong to [0,5), keeping their original order and excluding the event at 5.
data-stream-windows.why: Membership must follow timestamps and the declared interval, independent of arrival order.

data-artifact-lineage.name: Both dependencies changed together
data-artifact-lineage.prompt: The requested dataset and transformation versions have both moved on. Predict reuse without assuming only one dependency can fail at a time.
data-artifact-lineage.why: The combined check must preserve simultaneous mismatches rather than treating a single changed field as the only possible case.

databricks-lazy-dataframes.name: The valid boundary moves to a different column
databricks-lazy-dataframes.prompt: The minimum now applies to pressure. Return the requested fields from the new batch without changing the source.
databricks-lazy-dataframes.why: The rule reads the supplied field and preserves a value exactly on the boundary.

databricks-shuffle-skew.name: A different pump sends an uneven burst
databricks-shuffle-skew.prompt: Five B records and one A arrive. Split B over three salt groups and route to three workers with the declared hash.
databricks-shuffle-skew.why: Changing the dominant key and worker count tests the routing rule rather than a copied balanced list.

databricks-delta-snapshots.name: A new correction arrives while the older run is inspected
databricks-delta-snapshots.prompt: Versions 2 and 3 are retained, but the report names version 2. Return the pressure mean for that version.
databricks-delta-snapshots.why: A later extreme correction must not redefine the declared historical input.

databricks-replay-safe-ingest.name: A replay arrives beside a new empty file
databricks-replay-safe-ingest.prompt: File b is already committed; file c is new and empty. Preserve the rows and record c as completed.
databricks-replay-safe-ingest.why: A genuine new input can change progress without changing the output row count.

databricks-change-data-capture.name: Another entity changes while an old pump update returns
databricks-change-data-capture.prompt: A is already deleted at sequence 6. Ignore its incoming sequence 5 update while accepting B at sequence 2.
databricks-change-data-capture.why: A stale update and a useful update can share one batch; reject the former without dropping the latter.

databricks-lakeflow-quality.name: A different field passes exactly at its boundary
databricks-lakeflow-quality.prompt: Pressure values are 4,5 and null. With a minimum of 5, drop only failing records and publish the accepted candidate.
databricks-lakeflow-quality.why: A changed field and an exact-boundary value test the predicate and policy independently.

databricks-mlflow-lineage.name: Matching version numbers hide a different table
databricks-mlflow-lineage.prompt: Select on lab.validation.sensor_readings version 6, split holdout-A. The low-error run uses another table with the same version and split. Keep the requested assessment identity while allowing a different training table.
databricks-mlflow-lineage.why: The version belongs to one table. The selected run keeps its distinct training identity while sharing the requested assessment evidence.

databricks-unity-catalog-access.name: The short table name stays the same in another schema
databricks-unity-catalog-access.prompt: The job has catalog usage and SELECT on lab.other.features, but schema usage is granted only on lab.training. Return the missing requirement.
databricks-unity-catalog-access.why: A privilege on the earlier schema does not satisfy the new object boundary.

databricks-historical-features.name: One pump is stale while another has just published
databricks-historical-features.prompt: At minute 8, A’s minute-5 value is too old for a two-minute limit and its next value arrives at 9. B has a value at 8. Preserve both prediction rows.
databricks-historical-features.why: Missingness belongs to the particular prediction; a different entity’s fresh value cannot repair it.

systems-inference-batching.name: A partial batch leaves on its delay limit
systems-inference-batching.prompt: Two images arrive at 2 and 7 ms, dispatch at 9, and finish after 4 ms of execution. Predict both latencies before changing the waiting policy.
systems-inference-batching.why: A partial batch still has a common completion and distinct per-request waits.

systems-agent-deadlines.name: The run is already overdue
systems-agent-deadlines.prompt: The overall budget is 500 ms, elapsed time is 600 ms, and 50 ms was reserved for the response. Predict the new-call allowance.
systems-agent-deadlines.why: An overdue run must not turn a negative remainder into a fresh positive timeout.

systems-kv-cache-memory.name: Several sequences end while a new one grows
systems-kv-cache-memory.prompt: Two sequences are now empty and one retains 12 tokens. Predict dense cache bytes without charging for completed sequences.
systems-kv-cache-memory.why: Admission estimates must use current retained tokens rather than a fixed number of conversations.

systems-context-cache.name: The context matches but the question changes
systems-context-cache.prompt: The same team uses the same evidence snapshot, but asks a new question. Predict reuse before checking either comparison branch.
systems-context-cache.why: Context equality alone is insufficient; the actual question remains a required dependency.

serving-prefill-decode.name: A prompt starts sooner but decoding stalls
serving-prefill-decode.prompt: The next trace arrives at 20 ms and emits at [60,80,150,170] ms. Predict the first wait and every later gap separately.
serving-prefill-decode.why: A shorter initial wait does not remove a long pause inside the stream.

serving-prefix-reuse.name: The next team sends the same tokens
serving-prefix-reuse.prompt: All tokens and model versions match, but the incoming tenant namespace is different. Predict the reusable-token count under the stated isolation policy.
serving-prefix-reuse.why: A cross-namespace match still fails this explicit application contract.

serving-continuous-admission.name: A longer output allowance fills the remaining cache
serving-continuous-admission.prompt: B still owns two of six blocks. Two slots are free. C reserves four blocks and D reserves one. Predict the new admissions under strict FIFO.
serving-continuous-admission.why: Two free slots do not permit D after C consumes the remaining block allowance.

serving-cancellation-pressure.name: One release arrives during a new burst
serving-cancellation-pressure.prompt: A is now acknowledged; B still owns four blocks. One request already waits and three arrive with a queue limit of three. Predict both ownership and queue outcomes.
serving-cancellation-pressure.why: Confirmed release changes the held reservation while the independent waiting limit still rejects the overflow.

serving-canary-effects.name: The candidate now handles every request
serving-canary-effects.prompt: With 100 percent candidate traffic, one run is a shadow and another lacks write capability. Predict the named write decisions without treating candidate routing as permission.
serving-canary-effects.why: Changing rollout share does not change the independent effect-authority rule.

robot-perception-frames.name: A clockwise camera observes another point
robot-perception-frames.prompt: The camera-to-robot rotation is now clockwise and the offset is negative on one axis. Predict the robot-frame point before applying the two operations.
robot-perception-frames.why: Changed rotation direction and offset expose memorised coordinates and incorrect operation order.

robot-observation-latency.name: Motion on both axes during a shorter delay
robot-observation-latency.prompt: The part now moves in two directions. Predict its current position after half a second, keeping the two coordinates distinct and starting from the supplied captured position.
robot-observation-latency.why: The same update must handle vector motion and signs rather than a hard-coded conveyor axis.

robot-feedback-corrections.name: Correct from the other side of the target
robot-feedback-corrections.prompt: Botie begins beyond the target. Predict the next position with a half-second update and verify that the command points back toward the target.
robot-feedback-corrections.why: The sign of the measured error must control direction; a fixed positive movement is not feedback.

robot-actuator-windup.name: A smaller timestep changes the stored correction
robot-actuator-windup.prompt: The command request still saturates, but the update interval is now half a second. Predict both the applied command and the next integral contribution.
robot-actuator-windup.why: The instantaneous clipped command stays the same while the time-integrated memory update shrinks.

state-predict-correct.name: A reversed measurement pulls the next prediction back
state-predict-correct.prompt: The earlier mean is-1m, displacement3m, earlier variance2 m² and added motion variance2 m². The new measurement is1m with variance 4 m². Predict both corrected quantities.
state-predict-correct.why: The same gain must handle either innovation sign while keeping variance separate from position.

state-missing-observations.name: A longer reverse interval follows the missed frame
state-missing-observations.prompt: Start at mean1m and variance0.5m². The two displacements are-1m and-2 m, with added variances0.5m² and1 m². Only the final measurement arrives, at-1m with variance 1 m². Predict the final state.
state-missing-observations.why: Unequal intervals and reversed motion expose a reset or a fabricated zero measurement.

state-gating-association.name: A more uncertain prediction accepts a larger raw displacement
state-gating-association.prompt: The prediction is0 m with variance 4 m². Candidate positions are[-2,10]m, R is1 m² and the squared-distance gate is1. Predict the final estimate after resolving the candidate.
state-gating-association.why: Scaling by combined uncertainty changes what a raw displacement means, while the exact-one association rule still applies.

state-model-uncertainty.name: The next camera reading has a different error
state-model-uncertainty.prompt: Initial mean0 m and variance0.5m², expected displacement1m and Q0.5m² produce a prior. The observation is4 m with R1 m²; independent reference is3m. Predict the completed estimate and its diagnostic without leaking that reference into the update.
state-model-uncertainty.why: A different observation error checks the separated estimation/evaluation paths; its covered reference remains one diagnostic example.

security-retrieval-authority.name: The requester changes tenant
security-retrieval-authority.prompt: The same candidates are now evaluated for tenant B, and one B document lacks a grant. Predict which IDs remain without reusing the previous caller’s mask.
security-retrieval-authority.why: Authorisation belongs to the current request and current grants, not a cached global relevance result.

security-private-aggregates.name: A narrower public range with four people
security-private-aggregates.prompt: The declared bounds are now [1,5] and four people contribute [0,2,4,10]. Predict both outputs using those bounds rather than the observed minimum and maximum.
security-private-aggregates.why: The sensitivity depends on the public range and fixed number of people, even when observations fall outside both bounds.

security-model-artifacts.name: The loader passes while every digest fails
security-model-artifacts.prompt: Both candidates have approved loading formats but fail trusted byte verification. Predict the allowed IDs without treating format approval as provenance.
security-model-artifacts.why: An acceptable loader does not repair an artifact whose bytes differ from the trusted expectation.

security-training-provenance.name: Neither proposal is ready for this release
security-training-provenance.prompt: One row has a reviewed label from an unapproved source; another comes from the approved source without completed review. Predict the accepted IDs and mean.
security-training-provenance.why: Independent requirements cannot be satisfied by different records or by treating an empty fit as zero.

security-backdoor-evaluation.name: One clean prediction was already wrong
security-backdoor-evaluation.prompt: Predict both report branches when one faulty example was already classified safe before the supplied change.
security-backdoor-evaluation.why: The clean error and true target-class example must not inflate the newly induced target-success denominator.

security-adversarial-threat-models.name: The same size change reaches a protected coordinate
security-adversarial-threat-models.prompt: The new supplied input changes only the second coordinate. Predict the complete report rather than counting its wrong label as a permitted failure.
security-adversarial-threat-models.why: A numerical change budget cannot override the independent restriction on which measurements the opponent controls.

security-prediction-api-controls.name: The batch exactly fits the caller’s remaining rows
security-prediction-api-controls.prompt: The caller has used 8 of 10 rows. A 2-row batch costs 2 units per row, and 5 global units remain. Predict the admitted public response for score 0.2 and cutoff 0.5.
security-prediction-api-controls.why: An inclusive capacity boundary should admit a fitting batch while the response still withholds the internal score.

simulation-time-steps.name: A different ambient temperature and a shorter step
simulation-time-steps.prompt: The pump is now at 40, ambient is 10, the rate is 0.2 and timestep is 0.5. Predict one Euler update without reusing the old cooling difference.
simulation-time-steps.why: The update must respond to the current excess temperature, rate and physical interval.

simulation-paired-trials.name: A candidate loses on most of the new shifts
simulation-paired-trials.prompt: The candidate reduces cost on one shift but raises it on two. Predict the mean gain and decide which individual changes you would inspect next.
simulation-paired-trials.why: A paired comparison must retain negative gains and cannot assume a candidate is always an improvement.

simulation-system-identification.name: A different command scale tests the fitted rule
simulation-system-identification.prompt: The commands are [2,4] and responses [3,6]. Predict the estimated gain while keeping the units and through-origin model unchanged.
simulation-system-identification.why: The estimator must respond to the command scale rather than averaging the response values.

simulation-transfer-checks.name: Two moderate failures replace one extreme failure
simulation-transfer-checks.prompt: The new costs are [7,9,9,3]. Predict mean and worst tested cost, then consider how the failure count differs from the earlier single difficult condition.
simulation-transfer-checks.why: A lower maximum can coexist with more failing conditions; preserve per-condition evidence beyond both summary values.

numerical-stable-normalisation.name: A signed embedding arrives at an even larger scale
numerical-stable-normalisation.prompt: Botie receives [0,-5e250]. Predict the direction before running the repaired graph. Neither the sign nor the zero coordinate should disappear.
numerical-stable-normalisation.why: A stable calculation preserves direction, including its sign, across numerical scales.

numerical-identifiable-models.name: A different unresolved gain pair changes the useful experiment
numerical-identifiable-models.prompt: The candidates are [1,1] and [1,2]. The proposed rows are [[1,0],[0,2],[1,1]], and the minimum planning gap is 1.5. Predict which original position survives.
numerical-identifiable-models.why: A useful experiment depends on the specific competing parameter difference and the instrument’s declared resolution.

numerical-gradient-checks.name: The corner moves with the target
numerical-gradient-checks.prompt: The absolute test loss now has target 3 and is checked at weight 3 with step 0.25. Predict the two sides and their central estimate. A shifted target does not remove the corner.
numerical-gradient-checks.why: The checker must follow the actual loss and its target, rather than assuming the only problematic point is numerical zero.

numerical-adaptive-steps.name: A faster cooling rate exposes a shorter acceptable interval
numerical-adaptive-steps.prompt: Botie now starts at excess temperature four with rate one per second and proposed interval 0.2 seconds. Absolute tolerance is 0.01 and relative tolerance is zero. Predict the report before running it.
numerical-adaptive-steps.why: Changing the dynamics changes the numerical disagreement; the old accepted interval is not a universal property of the simulator.
